description: This module allows you to add, remove or modify Keycloak identity providers using the Keycloak REST API. It requires access to the REST API using OpenID Connect; the user connecting and the client being used must have the requisite access rights. In a default Keycloak installation, admin-cli and an admin user would work, as would a separate client definition with the scope tailored to your needs and a user having the expected roles.

parameters.name: add_read_token_role_on_create
parameters.description: Enable/disable whether new users can read any stored tokens. This assigns the broker.read-token role. Choices: false true

parameters.name: alias
parameters.description: The alias uniquely identifies an identity provider and it is also used to build the redirect URI.

parameters.name: auth_client_id
parameters.description: OpenID Connect client_id to authenticate to the API with. Default: "admin-cli"

parameters.name: auth_client_secret
parameters.description: Client Secret to use in conjunction with auth_client_id (if required).

parameters.name: auth_keycloak_url
parameters.description: URL to the Keycloak instance.

parameters.name: auth_password
parameters.description: Password to authenticate for API access with.

parameters.name: auth_realm
parameters.description: Keycloak realm name to authenticate to for API access.

parameters.name: auth_username
parameters.description: Username to authenticate for API access with.

parameters.name: authenticate_by_default
parameters.description: Specifies if this identity provider should be used by default for authentication even before displaying login screen. Choices: false true

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: Dict specifying the configuration options for the provider; the contents differ depending on the value of provider_id. Examples are given below for oidc and saml. It is easiest to obtain valid config values by dumping an already-existing identity provider configuration through check-mode in the existing field.

parameters.name: connection_timeout
parameters.description: Controls the HTTP connections timeout period (in seconds) to Keycloak API. Default: 10

parameters.name: display_name
parameters.description: Friendly name for identity provider.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Enable/disable this identity provider. Choices: false true

parameters.name: first_broker_login_flow_alias
parameters.description: Alias of authentication flow, which is triggered after first login with this identity provider.

parameters.name: http_agent
parameters.description: Configures the HTTP User-Agent header. Default: "Ansible"

parameters.name: link_only
parameters.description: If true, users cannot log in through this provider. They can only link to this provider. This is useful if you do not want to allow login from the provider, but want to integrate with a provider. Choices: false true

parameters.name: mappers
parameters.description: A list of dicts defining mappers associated with this Identity Provider.

parameters.name: post_broker_login_flow_alias
parameters.description: Alias of authentication flow, which is triggered after each login with this identity provider.

parameters.name: provider_id
parameters.description: Protocol used by this provider (supported values are oidc or saml).

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: The Keycloak realm under which this identity provider resides. Default: "master"

parameters.name: refresh_token
parameters.description: Authentication refresh token for Keycloak API.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: State of the identity provider. On present, the identity provider is created if it does not yet exist, or updated with the parameters you provide. On absent, the identity provider is removed if it exists. Choices: "present" ← (default) "absent"

parameters.name: store_token
parameters.description: Enable/disable whether tokens must be stored after authenticating users. Choices: false true

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Authentication token for Keycloak API.

parameters.name: trust_email
parameters.description: If enabled, email provided by this provider is not verified even if verification is enabled for the realm. Choices: false true

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: Verify TLS certificates (do not disable this in production). Choices: false true ← (default)

examples:
- name: Create OIDC identity provider, authentication with credentials
  community.general.keycloak_identity_provider:
    state: present
    auth_keycloak_url: https://auth.example.com/auth
    auth_realm: master
    auth_username: admin
    auth_password: admin
    realm: myrealm
    alias: oidc-idp
    display_name: OpenID Connect IdP
    enabled: true
    provider_id: oidc
    config:
      issuer: https://idp.example.com
      authorizationUrl: https://idp.example.com/auth
      tokenUrl: https://idp.example.com/token
      userInfoUrl: https://idp.example.com/userinfo
      clientAuthMethod: client_secret_post
      clientId: my-client
      clientSecret: secret
      syncMode: FORCE
    mappers:
      - name: first_name
        identityProviderMapper: oidc-user-attribute-idp-mapper
        config:
          claim: first_name
          user.attribute: first_name
          syncMode: INHERIT
      - name: last_name
        identityProviderMapper: oidc-user-attribute-idp-mapper
        config:
          claim: last_name
          user.attribute: last_name
          syncMode: INHERIT

- name: Create OIDC identity provider, with well-known configuration URL
  community.general.keycloak_identity_provider:
    state: present
    auth_keycloak_url: https://auth.example.com/auth
    auth_realm: master
    auth_username: admin
    auth_password: admin
    realm: myrealm
    alias: oidc-idp
    display_name: OpenID Connect IdP
    enabled: true
    provider_id: oidc
    config:
      fromUrl: https://the-idp.example.com/auth/realms/idprealm/.well-known/openid-configuration
      clientAuthMethod: client_secret_post
      clientId: my-client
      clientSecret: secret

- name: Create SAML identity provider, authentication with credentials
  community.general.keycloak_identity_provider:
    state: present
    auth_keycloak_url: https://auth.example.com/auth
    auth_realm: master
    auth_username: admin
    auth_password: admin
    realm: myrealm
    alias: saml-idp
    display_name: SAML IdP
    enabled: true
    provider_id: saml
    config:
      entityId: https://auth.example.com/auth/realms/myrealm
      singleSignOnServiceUrl: https://idp.example.com/login
      wantAuthnRequestsSigned: true
      wantAssertionsSigned: true
    mappers:
      - name: roles
        identityProviderMapper: saml-user-attribute-idp-mapper
        config:
          user.attribute: roles
          attribute.friendly.name: User Roles
          attribute.name: roles
          syncMode: INHERIT

- name: Create OIDC identity provider, authentication with credentials and advanced claim to group
  community.general.keycloak_identity_provider:
    state: present
    auth_keycloak_url: https://auth.example.com/auth
    auth_realm: master
    auth_username: admin
    auth_password: admin
    realm: myrealm
    alias: oidc-idp
    display_name: OpenID Connect IdP
    enabled: true
    provider_id: oidc
    config:
      issuer: https://idp.example.com
      authorizationUrl: https://idp.example.com/auth
      tokenUrl: https://idp.example.com/token
      userInfoUrl: https://idp.example.com/userinfo
      clientAuthMethod: client_secret_post
      clientId: my-client
      clientSecret: secret
      syncMode: FORCE
    mappers:
      - name: group_name
        identityProviderMapper: oidc-advanced-group-idp-mapper
        config:
          claims: '[{"key":"my_key","value":"my_value"}]'
          group: group_name
          syncMode: INHERIT

return_values.name: end_state
return_values.description: Representation of identity provider after module execution. Returned: on success Sample: {"addReadTokenRoleOnCreate": false, "alias": "my-idp", "authenticateByDefault": false, "config": {"authorizationUrl": "https://idp.example.com/auth", "clientAuthMethod": "client_secret_post", "clientId": "my-client", "clientSecret": "**********", "issuer": "https://idp.example.com", "tokenUrl": "https://idp.example.com/token", "userInfoUrl": "https://idp.example.com/userinfo"}, "displayName": "OpenID Connect IdP", "enabled": true, "firstBrokerLoginFlowAlias": "first broker login", "internalId": "4d28d7e3-1b80-45bb-8a30-5822bf55aa1c", "linkOnly": false, "providerId": "oidc", "storeToken": false, "trustEmail": false}

return_values.name: existing
return_values.description: Representation of existing identity provider. Returned: always Sample: {"addReadTokenRoleOnCreate": false, "alias": "my-idp", "authenticateByDefault": false, "config": {"authorizationUrl": "https://old.example.com/auth", "clientAuthMethod": "client_secret_post", "clientId": "my-client", "clientSecret": "**********", "issuer": "https://old.example.com", "syncMode": "FORCE", "tokenUrl": "https://old.example.com/token", "userInfoUrl": "https://old.example.com/userinfo"}, "displayName": "OpenID Connect IdP", "enabled": true, "firstBrokerLoginFlowAlias": "first broker login", "internalId": "4d28d7e3-1b80-45bb-8a30-5822bf55aa1c", "linkOnly": false, "providerId": "oidc", "storeToken": false, "trustEmail": false}

return_values.name: msg
return_values.description: Message as to what action was taken. Returned: always Sample: "Identity provider my-idp has been created"

return_values.name: proposed
return_values.description: Representation of proposed identity provider. Returned: always Sample: {"config": {"authorizationUrl": "https://idp.example.com/auth", "clientAuthMethod": "client_secret_post", "clientId": "my-client", "clientSecret": "secret", "issuer": "https://idp.example.com", "tokenUrl": "https://idp.example.com/token", "userInfoUrl": "https://idp.example.com/userinfo"}, "displayName": "OpenID Connect IdP", "providerId": "oidc"}
